name: Dusky Rose
lede: Dusky Rose is a muted, dusty rose-red, a name for a pink with some brown or mauve in it.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
The name comes from the xkcd survey of 2010, and our sources record nothing earlier under these words [1]. Its nearest named neighbor is [[mauve]], about 10 units away, and it is also near [[old-rose]] [1].

Books use the phrase for clothing. In *Fabric*, Finlay recalls a christening photograph in which her mother wears a blue suit of the 1960s and a dusky rose hat [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our archive a color near this swatch appears in 34 of 23,781 paintings, or 0.14 per cent, which is rarer than 67 per cent of the named colors [3]. In a painting it most often plays an accent [3]. The earliest match dates from the year 1000, a thousand years before the name was first recorded, so it is a look-alike hue in an aged photograph, not proof of a pigment [3].
